vision: Build a multi-tenant jewellery management SaaS with inventory, billing, branch management, offline synchronization, role-based access, PostgreSQL, and an administrative dashboard.

nonfunctional.text: Clients keep working without connectivity and synchronize when back online.
Every API checks the caller's role; the UI hides actions a role cannot perform.
Tenant data is isolated: no query may return another tenant's rows.

acceptance_criteria.text: Suggested: an authorized user can complete the 'Inventory' workflow end to end, and an unauthorized user is refused.
Suggested: an authorized user can complete the 'Billing' workflow end to end, and an unauthorized user is refused.

assumptions.text: Single region deployment initially; multi-region is out of scope.
The generated tables, endpoints and non-functional requirements are starting points inferred from keywords, not stated requirements.
Tenants are isolated by a tenant_id column in one database.
Offline conflicts resolve last-write-wins per record using server timestamps.

open_questions: How many users and requests per second do you expect at launch and in a year?
Are there compliance or data-residency requirements?
How should conflicting offline edits to the same record be resolved?
How long must data be retained, and when must it be deleted?

decisions.title: API gateway as the single public entry point
decisions.rationale: Keeps internal services private and centralizes TLS, auth checks and rate limits.
decisions.tradeoffs: Adds a hop and a component to operate.

decisions.title: PostgreSQL as the system of record
decisions.rationale: Relational integrity and transactions for core data.
decisions.tradeoffs: Requires schema migrations; scale reads with replicas before sharding.

decisions.title: Shared database, tenant_id on every row
decisions.rationale: Simplest multi-tenant model to operate; isolation is enforced by tenant-scoped queries (optionally Postgres row-level security).
decisions.tradeoffs: A missing tenant filter leaks data; noisy tenants share capacity.

decisions.title: Offline-first clients with a sync endpoint
decisions.rationale: Clients queue changes locally and push them in batches.
decisions.tradeoffs: Requires conflict resolution and idempotent change ids.
